source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: The lecture-recording-to-lecture-notes skill bundles real Python scripts, such as one that pulls frames out of a video, rather than asking the model to extract frames on its own. Why does this design make sense?

options.text: Because Python is the language a skill's bundled code has to be written in
options.feedback: Skills are not tied to one language. Python shows up here because it fits the job of pulling frames out of a video file, not because the skill format demands it.

options.text: Because a bundled script handles the whole job, leaving the model nothing to interpret
options.feedback: The skill still needs the model to work out what a phrase like "as you can see" is pointing at. The script covers one mechanical step; it does not cover the task.

options.text: Because a script written once will not need revising as the rest of the skill changes
options.feedback: Nothing suggests a script is frozen once written. A skill's code can be revised like any other part of it, the way the class proposed revising its narrative-versus-expository instruction.

options.text: Because code does the mechanical extraction reliably, leaving the model to interpret what it means
options.feedback: Ordinary software handles the reliable, mechanical step of grabbing a frame at a given timestamp, while the model supplies the judgment about what that material means in context. Each side does the part it is actually good at.
